differences.title: 1. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Kubernetes has a steeper learning curve but offers immense power and flexibility.
differences.rightDesc: Docker Swarm is significantly easier to learn and set up for basic orchestration needs.

differences.title: 2. FEATURES
differences.leftDesc: Rich features: autoscaling, self-healing, advanced load balancing, and a vast ecosystem.
differences.rightDesc: Core orchestration features: scaling, rolling updates, service discovery, and load balancing.

differences.title: 3. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Designed for large-scale, complex deployments and enterprise-level container management.
differences.rightDesc: Suitable for small to medium-sized applications, scales well but not to K8s levels.

differences.title: 4. ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Huge community support, numerous integrations, tools, and a rich add-on marketplace.
differences.rightDesc: Relies heavily on the Docker ecosystem; fewer dedicated Swarm-specific extensions.

differences.title: 5. IMPLEMENTATION
differences.leftDesc: Requires careful planning and often involves multiple components for a full cluster.
differences.rightDesc: Integrated directly into Docker Engine, very straightforward to initialize and manage.

differences.title: 6. COMMUNITY
differences.leftDesc: Backed by CNCF, with a massive, active, and diverse global developer community.
differences.rightDesc: Smaller community, primarily users of the Docker platform.

differences.title: 7. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for microservices, large-scale apps, CI/CD, and mission-critical workloads.
differences.rightDesc: Great for development, testing, and small-to-medium production environments.
